assertion: An event exists, described as "Oil price sharp fall due to US-Iran attack pause".
judge_quote: The price of oil has fallen sharply on hopes that a pause in attacks between the US and Iran could help to de‑escalate the conflict.
evidence_cited: The price of oil has fallen sharply on hopes that a pause in attacks between the US and Iran could help to de-escalate the conflict.
Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point, marking a sharp turnaround from last week when it had risen above $100.
The fall came after the US ambassador to the UN said attacks on Iran had been halted for a second night in a row to give "talks some space".
An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response.

evidence_cited: The outbreak of the Iran war triggered a sharp rise in oil prices as the conflict led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route which usually carries about 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG).
